summary: Memory-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) policies are meant to remember what happened. Many of them, however, fill memory by time: they sample frames uniformly across the episode and stamp each frame with its time step.
takeaways: Such a null event changes nothing the task depends on, yet a released memory VLA counts the interval as work done and stops early.
Across RoboMME's released designs, vulnerability follows how memory is indexed.
Many of them, however, fill memory by time: they sample frames uniformly across the episode and stamp each frame with its time step.
